register.name: Hurricane Beryl response plan, Grenada and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
register.detail: United Nations and partners · launched 10 July 2024 · a $9 million plan for the two nations · FAO, ILO, IOM, ITU, OCHA, UN Women, UNICEF and WFP
register.note: Shelter, food and health care among the top priorities; about 43,000 people in the two nations
register.text: The response plan of the United Nations and its partners after Hurricane Beryl, of which $4 million is for Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, for about 43,000 people in the two nations together. The partners named shelter, food and health care among the top priorities: it serves food, the standard furthest from reach, with shelter and health.

register.name: Strengthening Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Health Threats in the OECS Region
register.detail: World Bank, from the Pandemic Fund · grant approved 9 May 2025 · P509060 · closing 31 March 2028 · Dominica, Grenada, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
register.note: The nation’s share of a US$2,247,448 grant for four OECS nations
register.text: A Pandemic Fund grant, administered by the World Bank, to strengthen surveillance and diagnostic capacity in four OECS nations through a One Health approach. In Saint Vincent and the Grenadines it is implemented by the Public Sector Investment Project Management Unit of the Ministry of Finance, with the Ministry of Health, Wellness and the Environment leading activities; it serves the health standard.

register.name: Caribbean Resilient Renewable Energy Infrastructure Investment Facility (RREIIF)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 17 April 2025 · P180831 · Grenada, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines · signing ceremony 11 July 2025 · closing 31 December 2032 · US$29.3 million for the nation (World Bank FinancesOne)
register.note: The nation’s part of a US$110 million regional facility; a target of 10 MW of renewable capacity in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
register.text: A regional World Bank facility of US$110 million that pools renewable energy projects across three nations to lower costs and attract private developers, reinforces transmission and distribution with battery storage, and uses partial credit guarantees to mobilise up to US$120 million of commercial credit. It serves the energy standard, with a target of 10 MW of renewable capacity in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

register.name: Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Financing with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approval announced 10 April 2025 · Cat DDO, a fast-access line of credit for disasters
register.note: Reforms include a national disaster management policy, school safety protocols and modern rules for land use and environmental assessment
register.text: IDA financing of US$20 million with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option, a fast-access line of credit when a disaster strikes, approved after Hurricane Beryl, whose economic damage was estimated at US$230.6 million, 22 percent of 2023 GDP. It supports reforms in disaster risk management, land use and school safety, serving the shelter and education standards.

register.name: Beryl Emergency Resilient Recovery Project (BERRy)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 17 October 2024 · P507316 · income support, small-business grants, cash for work and resilient rebuilding
register.note: Over 5,200 households paid income support by mid-2025; more than 35 school renovations reimbursed
register.text: An IDA operation of US$63 million to restore incomes and rebuild after Hurricane Beryl, with temporary income grants for affected households, grants and support for small businesses, cash-for-work jobs and the repair of water systems and public buildings to withstand future hazards. By January 2026 it had reimbursed over US$9 million for more than 35 school renovations, serving the livelihood, education and water standards.

register.name: Basic Needs Trust Fund, eleventh programme (BNTF 11)
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · release of 23 October 2026 · with the Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines · over four years
register.note: More than 700 Vincentians expected to benefit
register.text: The Caribbean Development Bank’s community programme in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, of approximately US$4 million over four years. Its sub-projects include footpaths, stairs, drainage and retaining walls in Golden Vale and Acres Hill, and education infrastructure at Canouan Primary School, serving the shelter and education standards.
by: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

register.name: Hurricane Beryl relief package
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · approved after Hurricane Beryl, as for Grenada · grant and concessional loan financing · reported at the Bank’s annual news conference, 19 March 2025
register.note: For Grenada and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines together, the Bank gave US$10 million of concessional Immediate Response Loans and US$600,000 of grants
register.text: A relief package of US$5.5 million approved by the Caribbean Development Bank for Saint Vincent and the Grenadines after Hurricane Beryl. The Bank offered grant and concessional loan financing for the most urgent needs, among them damage to power, health and social service facilities, serving the energy, health and livelihood standards.

register.name: Strengthening response and resilience in the health sector
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · approved December 2022 · approved total $4,603,000 · under implementation, project page updated 19 November 2026
register.note: Surveillance, case detection and critical care services
register.text: A Caribbean Development Bank operation to boost the capacity of public healthcare in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines for COVID-19 related challenges and other emergencies, through increased surveillance, case detection and critical care services. Approved in 2022 and still under implementation, it serves the health standard.

register.name: Safety Nets for Vulnerable Populations
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · approved December 2021 · approved total $7,725,800 · under implementation, project page updated 19 November 2026
register.note: A minimum quality of life for vulnerable populations, with incomes and jobs maintained
register.text: A Caribbean Development Bank operation to ensure a minimum quality of life for vulnerable populations in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, maintain income and employment levels while preserving essential human capital, and improve educational continuity. Approved in 2021 and still under implementation, it serves the livelihood and education standards.

register.name: Social relief grant
register.detail: Republic of China (Taiwan) · signed 3 February 2026 · EC$8,064,600
register.note: To support families, strengthen communities and reinforce social institutions
register.text: A grant of US$3 million (EC$8,064,600) from the Republic of China (Taiwan) to the Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, signed on 3 February 2026. The Government states that it will be used to support families, strengthen communities and reinforce social institutions across the country; it serves the livelihood standard.

enterprises.heading: Already working in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

items.name: Eco Home Gardens
items.text: A women-led home and community gardening project that farms organically and turns surplus harvests into ginger and turmeric powders, grated coconut, fruit blends and crystallised ginger, already sold at home and abroad, building the capacity of more than 100 women in organic farming.
